title: TAMARIND AND LEMON. (the nameplate gets the whole afternoon. these are brushed on purpose.)
format: carousel, 5 slides at 1080x1440: S1 video loop 10.0 s (300 frames, frame 0 = the cover = the grid tile, frame 299 leading into frame 0 by one ordinary step, soft baked foley), S2 video loop 7.0 s (210 frames, same seam rule, one baked cloth rub), S3-S5 stills
date: Fri 6 Nov 2026 (Dhanteras; never dated on any image)
caption:
Tamarind and lemon: the whole afternoon before Diwali goes to the brass nameplate. Every flat, every year.

The Brushed Gold Huggies skip that step: brushed to a soft satin, about 14 mm by 9.8 mm on a wide 6 mm band, so they scatter light instead of throwing it back. Listed as tarnish free. ₹999.

Gold coins are not sold here, downstairs or up. Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. The bag applies BUY2 or BUY3 for you. Shubh Dhanteras.

[ brushed gold huggies · 18k gold tone plated · no tamarind needed ]

alt_text: An illustrated pink Art Deco window in afternoon sun under a sage sunburst fanlight, a pink paper lantern turning beside it. In the apricot room: TAMARIND AND LEMON, 'the nameplate gets the whole afternoon. these are brushed on purpose.' Sun through the open window lies across the sill and the foot of the wall with the fanlight's shadow in it. On a folded white cloth on the sill sits a pair of chunky gold-tone huggie earrings with a soft brushed satin finish, their shadows falling back across the cloth. Below the window a polished brass plate carries the Naira wordmark and FLAT 102. In the loop, the soft reflection of a window across the street slides along the wall; on the polished plate the same window shows sharp, crossbars and all, with one sparkle, then the reflection climbs onto the sill, where the huggies only glow warmly, and fades away in the sun.

A close-up under the same window. On the sunlit sill stand the two brushed gold-tone huggies, the fanlight's shadow on the sunlit wall behind them; above them, on the apricot wall: THESE SKIP THIS STEP. 'brushed satin, not mirror. a soft dry cloth after you wear them.' Below, on the pink wall, the brass nameplate with the Naira wordmark and FLAT 102 starts dull and brown with tarnish, is polished bright in one slow sweep from left to right, holds while a soft warm sheen crosses the huggies, then slowly dulls again from the right.

Downstairs in Shop 1: an ivory shop under a wall tube light, framed by pink pilasters and sage shutter channels. A white tent card standing behind the tray reads GOLD COINS NOT SOLD HERE. On a blush velvet tray, standing clear on the glass counter with a brass edge and a teak front, sits the small pair of brushed gold-tone huggies. On the ivory counter front: '(18k gold tone plated, and we would rather say so today.)'

On apricot, the word SATIN. above the listing photograph: the two brushed gold-tone huggies on a white plaster cube in soft light, one standing and one on its side, framed by a thin gold line. Below: 'about 14 mm by 9.8 mm, a wide 6 mm band, brushed so it scatters light.'

The end card on apricot. A brass plate carries the Naira wordmark. Below it: FLAT 102 · FIRST FLOOR. BRUSHED GOLD HUGGIES. [ 18k gold tone plated ]. ₹999. 'brushed satin, not mirror.' nairaflore.com. every piece arrives in our blush box · free insured shipping · COD available.
sound: Baked, very soft, synthesised (nothing licensed; render/v3/p05/_build/sfx.py): S1 a far window latch at 0.5 s (the window opposite opening, peak -27 dBFS) and a faint bright ting at 2.4 s as the window crosses the plate (-23 dBFS), silence at the loop seam; S2 a soft cloth rub in five strokes over the polish, 0.5-2.6 s, the wipe's own timing (-26 dBFS). Optional in-app: a calm afternoon bansuri or sitar instrumental from the Instagram audio library, no vocals, ducked under the foley.
deviations: SIZE: the brief's 'about 12 mm across' is not in the listing. The live listing (Shopify, read 26 Oct) says 'about 14mm by 9.8mm with a wide flat band roughly 6mm deep'. S4 reads 'about 14 mm by 9.8 mm, a wide 6 mm band,' and the caption says 'About 14 mm by 9.8 mm on a wide 6 mm band'.

CAPTION: the middle paragraph is the review's text, word for word (hook, 'Gold coins' line, kicker and first comment unchanged). The care line left the caption because it is on S2 ('a soft dry cloth after you wear them.'); the brief's 'is all the care they ask' overstated the listing, whose care also keeps perfume off and stores them flat in the pouch, and it is no longer claimed anywhere. 'Listed as tarnish free' stays caption-only (tag Tarnish Free present). OFFER LINE (27 Oct, the executive creative director's P5 fix 1): the house sentence 'Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. The bag applies BUY2 or BUY3 for you.' now stands in the third paragraph, before 'Shubh Dhanteras.', word for word as the other eleven captions carry it. The brief left P5 the one caption without it ('Dhanteras is told straight'); Dhanteras is the season's biggest buying day, so that call is reversed. Caption only: no offer on any image.

THE FANLIGHT'S SHADOW does not fall across the huggies. The fan is the top of the window, so one sun lands its shadow furthest back: its arc and bar tips on the foot of the back wall (y 728-800), its bars, hub and transom across the back of the sill (y 800-850). The huggies stand at the front, in the sun. A shadow on the huggies needed a second, inconsistent light.

WORLD REVIEW FIX 5 (bay 5) applied, which moves the room off a flat apricot field. The room is painted in its sunlit colours with ONE shade multiply masked off the projected window. Measured on the cover: wall shade #E3B69E / sun #FEE4C1, Lab dL 14.3; sill shade #D9AB91 / sun #FDE1C0, dL 17.6. The sun direction is A .45 (was .25), further round to the left, so the huggies' own cast shadows clear their silhouettes and read; the jamb's shadow on the sill runs at the same angle. The wall band's top is y 728 (was 701), under the turn's descenders.

REFLECTION PATCH at 46 % at its heart, not 32 %: at 32 % it lifted the blush plaster by about 3 L and could not be followed on a phone. It carries a faint cross (the opposite window's bars). It is masked OFF the polished plate and the huggies. Inside the window opening it is now capped at 23 % everywhere, shade and sun alike, from 4.8 s (see FIX PASS 3, S1).

PATCH EXIT (review fix 1, applied as given): knots (6700,690,900),(7600,1110,905),(8200,1340,908) replaced by (6700,640,905),(7400,760,890); the patch's opacity falls 1 to 0 on a sine over 6.2-7.2 s, so it dies in the sun. Measured with the patch hidden vs shown: nothing lifts beyond x 800 at any frame, the right casement and pilaster (x > 930) get 0, and from 7.0 s the lift is under 2/255. 7.2-10.0 s is the quiet afternoon (2.8 s).

PLATE FLASH (review fix 3): the two white glass-glare streaks are gone. The flash is the patch's own rhomboid with its cross bars cut clean, blur 1 px, #FFF4DC at 60 % peak, screen, clipped to the plate and drawn inside the plate's SVG under its ink (the etched letters stay dark). Its x rides h.patchAt(t) with a gain of 1.65 (centred on the plate as the patch is at 2.5 s), so it crosses 2.1-2.9 s (centre x 312 to 636) at no more than 24 px a frame, and its y is the patch's own. The 16 % plate lift (2.1-2.5-2.9) and the ONE four-point sparkle at the upper right chamfer (fullest at 2.5 s) are kept. Light is this post's joke, where the brief allows sparkles. None on the huggies.

SATIN SHEEN, S1 and S2 (review fixes 2 and 6): colour #FFD98E, windows and band as given (S1 4.9-6.5 s; S2 380 px band, blur 40 px, 2.8-4.4 s on a sine). The blend is ADDED light (mix-blend-mode plus-lighter) at 16 % peak on S1 and 14 % on S2, not screen at 24 % with saturate(1.15) or soft-light, because the review's own acceptance test failed both: once the patch no longer fogged the gold, screen #FFD98E at 24 % measured saturation -4.4 % / -5.7 % with brightness only +1.9 % / +2.6 %; soft-light stayed under +3 %; saturate(1.15) round the pair pushed saturation +6-7 % and coloured the real piece. Light on gold comes back gold, so adding it in the gold's own hue brightens without fogging and without touching the cut-out. Measured at the peak against frame 0, HSV over each piece's own alpha: S1 (5.7 s) saturation -0.6 % / -2.0 %, brightness +5.2 % / +7.4 %; S2 (3.6 s) -0.9 % / -1.7 %, +5.9 % / +6.8 %. Left contrast now -7.6 % on S1 (was -22 %).

S2 DULL PLATE (review fix 4): the given recipe (saturate .85, brightness .74, #7A4E2C multiply 30 %) measured #765B35 on the brass (hue 34.8, darker than and still yellow of the review's target #8C6A44), so it is saturate(.75) brightness(1.02) with the #7A4E2C multiply at 50 %: brass mean (ink excluded) #8A6840, HSL S .37, hue 32.4; whole plate #84643E. The 14 tarnish clouds now sit at the four chamfers, the two screw heads and along the edges (radial falloff, 25 %), so the centre is a step lighter; the 18 % speckle stays warm brown.

S2 WIPES (review fix 5): E1 = PX+PW+170; the polish is a sine over 0.5-2.6 s (peak 25.7 px a frame), polished hold 2.6-5.4 s, the cloth rub re-timed to 0.5-2.6 s (five strokes). The reverse 5.4-7.0 s cannot be a plain sine under the 30 px cap: 1030 px in 1.6 s on a sine peaks at 33.7 px a frame. It uses sine ramps over its first and last quarter with a steady glide between (velocity C1-continuous, no jolt), peak 28.6 px a frame. The page at 7.0 s = the page at 0 s (max diff 0), so the 210-frame loop's last frame leads into frame 0 by one ordinary step.

S2 SUN ON THE BACK WALL (review fix 7): the band's edges are blurred 1.5 px (was 2.4) and S1's fanlight shadow is in it at 2x: 6 px bars and a 12 px arc, a warm brown (#6E3A26) multiply at 14 %, blur 0.7 px, clipped to the band. Four bars and the arc fall in the frame because the fan's apex is placed at x 1050; by S1's strict geometry it would sit just off this crop's right edge and only a sliver of arc would show.

SLIDE 2 LAYOUT: the upper part is the foot of 102's room (the apricot wall in shade with the sun's band behind the pieces) and the window's own inner sill, not plain blush facade. So the huggies' 'sill band' is a real sill and the slide reads as a close-up of slide 1. Below it, the outer sill and the row-3 plaster at 2x: the plate between the plate band's speed lines, the storey's bottom string course, the mortar joint, and row 4's top course. The huggies stand on the bare sill (the cloth is on the plate). The tarnish speckle is warm brown, not olive. The 5.4-7.0 reverse wipe carries no streak.

SLIDE 3: framed as P1 frames its shop (row-4 pilasters and piers, sage shutter channels, the rolled shutter's bottom slat overhead), the tube light wall-mounted at y 190-214. THE TENT CARD (review fix 8) stands on the glass BEHIND the tray: the tray is drawn again over its foot (the plate itself, clipped to the tray's silhouette traced off the photograph by the velvet's hue, run on down both rims to y 965); no drop shadow, a 6 px contact shadow (multiply 30 %) along the foot; turned 4 degrees as a shear (skewY(-4deg)) so its verticals stay plumb. Its geometry and the counter's are set out under FIX PASS 3, S3.

NIGHT_LIT / LIT (later establishing frames) deepened a step toward rose, with an OVERLAY lamp bloom (the kit's rule for lamps on a mid-dark room), so FLAT 102 reads at one third scale as a lit evening room between P4's lilac and P6's aubergine, not blush on blush. CLOSED is unchanged.

LOOP LENGTH (superseded 27 Oct by series fix S3, below): S1 shipped at 301 frames (10.033 s), the last a copy of frame 0, and S2 at 211, so the kandil held two frames at every wrap. Now S1 is 300 frames (10.0 s) and S2 210 (7.0 s), frame n at t = n / 30 s, the last frame leading into frame 0 by one ordinary step, one GOP at constant QP (feed/tools/reel.cjs --loop; p05/tools/loop.cjs hands its old command lines to it).

FIX PASS 3, S1 (director fix 1, the reflection patch's mask, world/bays/p05.js): (1) from 4.8 s the patch is capped at the sun's 23 % across the WHOLE window opening, in shade as well as in sun. The cap is a .p-cap rect in the patch mask on a sine ramp over 4.4-4.8 s, while the patch is still on the outer sill. (2) The shade/sun edges inside the room are feathered 12 px (sd 4.7, a 12 px 10-90 % rise). The opening's own edges keep the old 2 px blur, so the outer-sill crossing at 4.3-4.8 s is unchanged: outside the opening the old and new frames differ by at most 2 levels, and that is compositing noise. (3) The huggies' cut is dilated and feathered. DEVIATION: the given 8 px + 8 px (dilate 12, blur 2.5) still measured +9 / +10 at 17-20 px from the pair, in the dark gap between the pieces where both contact shadows lie, so it failed the acceptance. The feather runs 8 px further: dilate 16, blur 4 (98 % cut at 8 px, 50 % at 16, 16 % at 20). Result, measured with the patch shown vs hidden in the same frame, 100 ms steps, 3.8-7.3 s (_build/qa-patch.json): within 20 px of either huggie at most +6 (was +42), on the huggies 0 in every frame. In the director's cone box (x 430-520, y 815-880) the peak is +9 (was +33); it is now an even 23 % wash on the shaded plaster more than 20 px from the pair, no longer cut to the pair's silhouette. The #FFD98E sheen carries the beat alone. With h.fxOn off (every world render, sheet and establishing frame) the bay is pixel-identical to before (max diff 0 at t 0 and 5.8 s); CLOSED, OPENING(t), LIT and NIGHT_LIT are untouched.

FIX PASS 3, COVER: the patch is off the tile at t 0 (x -300), but its blend layer is composited in every frame of the loop, and the mask change re-composited the gradients under it by at most 2 levels (frame 0 vs the old cover@2x: max 2, nothing above 2). The shared world also moved since the cover was made. The cover was re-exported from the new S1 frame 0 at 2x (cover.jpg, cover-45.jpg, cover-thumb.png), so cover = slide 1 frame 0 stays exact; the image is visually unchanged. The layer is not toggled per beat, because switching it on or off would pop the gradients by 1-2 levels mid-loop.

FIX PASS 3, S2 (director fix 2): the pair is moved up 24 px, from y 480-707 to 456-683 (HY 456). Measured on the alpha: the right huggie's base is at y 669, 31 px inside the sill's lip (y 700); the left huggie's top is at y 469, 34 px under the turn's lowest ink (y 435). The contact shadows, the sun's cast shadows and the sheen's mask are keyed to HX / HY and moved with it. ADDED: the cast shadows are clipped to the sill (y 600-700). With the pair further back, the left one's shadow tip crossed the sill's back edge and showed as a dark notch on the wall. On slide 1's geometry that part falls on wall in shade, where a shadow cannot show. Re-rendered 7 s loop: the page at 7.0 s = frame 0 (decoded max diff 0, in the then 211-frame file; 210 frames since series fix S3).

FIX PASS 3, S3 (director fix 3, the tray against the channels): NOT applied as given, because the photograph does not allow it. AI-05 crops the tray: its front-right corner runs off the photo's right edge. The rims leave it at native x 2336, rows 870-1121, and the right rim's outer edge (+1.35) meets the front arris (-0.19) about 74 native px further on. So what read as the rim 'at x 955 against the channel at 958' was the photograph's cut, hidden by the channel. At 0.96 about x 540 the cut would land at x 943: the tray would end in the photo's own edge, sliced through its front rim, still running behind the right channel, with its true corner at about x 977. What was done instead meets the acceptance: the tray is COMPLETED and placed whole, clear of both channels. _build/AI-05-wide.png (tools/widen_ai05.py) rebuilds the tray's last 74 px and its corner from its own velvet: a per-column warp of its end columns between the three measured lines, shading from the warped columns, grain band-passed from real velvet at one random offset, the face darkening over its last 12 px, the corners rounded, the glass reflection and contact band carried under it and released round the corner. The counter is carried 100 px out on the left and 220 px on the right: the brass edges and band along their own slopes, the glass as a planar fit plus the photo's grain. The counter scene is at 0.9218 of P1's scale (the tray's true width is 2389 native px, so 0.96 cannot fit it with 16 px each side), centred on the tray's true centre at x 540, with the brass trim still ending at y 1220. Measured on the render: velvet x 145.0-934.5, clear of the left channel by 23.0 px and of the right by 23.5 px (_build/s03-check.json). The huggies stay at 0.62 (P1's 9 px/mm), centred on the tray at (540, 953). The tray clip over the card's foot is the same traced silhouette mapped to the new geometry and run on down both rims to y 965.

FIX PASS 3, S3, THE TENT CARD followed the smaller counter: at 760 wide its right end would have overhung the counter's right brass edge, which moved left and down with the scale. It is 730 wide at x 175-905, foot y 916 at x 540 (890.5 at x 905, 12 px inside the brass edge at y 878; 941.5 at x 175, 6 px inside the tray's left rim, so only the right foot shows, at x 834-905 on the glass). The type is Velista 80, not the brief's 84 (84 x 730/760, so 'NOT SOLD HERE.' keeps the brief's margins), baselines 540 / 632 (not 520 / 616), so the two lines sit centred in the card's visible part (y 360 to the tray's back rim at 758).

FIX PASS 3, S3 (director fix 4, the glass and the wedge; tools/s03_glass.py, built off a render of the slide with neither layer). GLASS: the #FBF3EC screen's strength is per pixel in _build/s03-glass-mask.png. The left glass (x < 300, below the tray rim) gets what it needs to reach #B9A187, smoothed and never under 20 %. The right glass and the strip in front of the tray get 23 %, so the sheet reads as one glass, blended over about 30 px. Cut out, feathered 1 px: the tray's whole footprint (the huggies inside it), the card and the wall, the brass edges and their gold reflections, the white light reflections, the glass's green edge. Measured on the final render (_build/s03-check.json): (170, 1000) reads #BDA68D (was #A38970). Over the left glass (x 152-300, outside the jamb's 30 px reveal shadow at x 122-152, beyond the tray's own 8 px contact shadow) the mean is #C0AA91, and 9 of 41,787 px are darker than #B9A187, all on the trim's edge row at y 1218 (the darkest, #A89A80). Inside the tray's soft 5-8 px contact shadow, 293 px are darker; they are kept because that shadow seats the tray on the glass. WEDGE: the wood face under the band is not screened (a 30 % ivory screen read milky). It is recoloured to the house teak in _build/s03-teak.png: each pixel takes #7A4836 (midway between #6B3A2A and #8A5A44) scaled by its own luminance over the wedge's mean, so the photo's brushed grain stays. Before mean #614223; after mean #7A4A37, 5-95 % #683F2E-#834F3B. The brass band (including its darker lower face) and its highlight are left as they are.

Motion speeds: the patch at most 17.6 px a frame; the plate's window image at most 24; S2's polish 25.7 and its reverse 28.6 (house cap 30). Scale: the huggies are the real cut-out (00-aa-trim, never upscaled): S1 0.96 (about 13.5 px/mm by the listing's 14 mm), S2 1.0 (about 14 px/mm, under the 16 px/mm 'shown larger' line), S3 0.62 (P1's 9 px/mm); S4 is the listing photo 02.jpg at 1.0. Each cut-out has contact shadows (multiply 28-46 %) and the drop shadow; no halo. The brushed gold is never recoloured or filtered: the sun's light lies UNDER it, and the sheen is added light in the gold's own hue, masked to its alpha, that comes and goes.

Type: Velista caps only (TAMARIND / AND LEMON., THESE / SKIP THIS STEP., GOLD COINS / NOT SOLD HERE., SATIN.), Cormorant turns lowercase ending in full stops, Jost on the end card with Poppins drawing the rupee sign. No em dash, no exclamation, NAIRA never set in type (the wordmark only: the plate on S1 and S2, the end card on S5; S3 and S4 carry none; one mark per frame). No type in any slide's top-right 173 x 202. Contrast (WCAG): S1 headline 9.2, turn 6.6; S2 9.2 / 6.5; S3 card 16.6, panel 10.6; S4 11.9 / 7.5; S5 11.4 / 7.3.
